title: Dedicated capacity: load validation playground and customer acceptance checklist
creator: Ava Moreno
description: Create a repeatable, end-to-end load validation playground for Dedicated capacity that (a) measures throughput guarantees against SLAs, (b) exercises autoscaling policies (scale-up, scale-down, cooldown, warm pools), and (c) provides a customer-facing acceptance test checklist and reporting template. This ticket covers harness design, canonical benchmark scenarios, runbooks for engineers and customers, and templates for pass/fail decisions. The goal is to produce a deterministic, reproducible methodology we can use for pre-sales validation, capacity commits, and quarterly SLA audits.
test_plan:
Overview:
1) Harness architecture: controller + workload generator + metrics collector + workload catalog (synthetic + sampled production traces). The controller orchestrates traffic ramps, applies autoscaler policy changes, and validates fallbacks.
2) Workloads: latency-sensitive single-turn generation, high-throughput batched token streams, mixed chat-style with KV cache warmup, and multi-tenant interference scenarios.
3) Warmup: each run includes a cache-priming phase (10 minutes) then a steady-state window (30 minutes) for measurements.
4) Sweep matrix: concurrency [1,4,8,16,32], request token lengths [8,64,512], batch sizes [1,8,32], KV-cache hit rate [0%, 50%, 90%], model variants [float32, int8-quant].
5) Autoscaler exercises: trigger scale-up with sustained queue > threshold for 45s, verify scale-down with cooldown of 120s, test warm-pool pre-warm and on-demand spin-up.
6) Failure cases: preempt a serving node, inject 10% CPU/GPU contention, enforce limited network egress to validate graceful degradation.
7) Reporting: generate a single run CSV + summary JSON (p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, GPU-util, queue length timeline, error rate).
Run instructions (engineer):
- Check out repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/dedicated-load-harness.git
- Create config in harness/configs/<customer-or-experiment>.yaml (example attached in artifacts).
- Start collector: ./harness/collect_metrics.sh --run-id=<id>
- Kick off controller: ./harness/controller.sh --config configs/<file> --run-id=<id>
- After run: ./harness/generate_report.sh --run-id=<id>
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end harness can run deterministically in CI or on a dedicated lab cluster and produce the summary JSON and CSV artifacts.

For a nominal dedicated unit (1 reserved node): p95 token latency for 64-token requests must be <= 350ms under the committed concurrency target, and tokens/sec matches the published throughput guarantee within ±7%.
Autoscaler behaviors validated: scale-up occurs within 60s of sustained queue crossing threshold; scale-down does not trigger during back-to-back bursts (cooldown respected).
Runbook includes a scripted customer acceptance checklist with explicit pass/fail criteria and remediation steps.
Artifacts (CSV, summary JSON, dashboard link) are uploaded to the run artifact bucket and a GitHub issue is created automatically with the run summary.
Documentation for how to replay a customer production trace in the harness is included and tested with one real trace sample (anonymized).
checklist: Design harness API and YAML config schema
Implement workload catalog: synthetic templates + trace replayer
Integrate metrics collector (Prometheus + GPU exporter + custom token-meter)
Implement controller that can apply autoscaler policy changes mid-run
Write customer-facing acceptance checklist and reporting template
Create CI job that runs a quick smoke scenario on each PR
Run full benchmark matrix for three model variants and upload artifacts
Write post-run analysis notebook and standard visualization set
